findings.title: Under --child-os wsl the DSN never crosses into WSL, so the DSN-level pin's exclusivity - which the ticket says is 'unchanged' - does not hold for the WSL-side node client, and AC3's respelled DSN reaches nothing
findings.evidence: Ticket line (Desired behavior): "`sslmode=verify-full` and the DSN-level pin's exclusivity are unchanged." And AC3: "the pinned DSN's `sslrootcert` carries the `/mnt/c/...` spelling". WHAT SHIPS: scripts/ops/dsn-pipe.mjs's WSL_ENV_LIST = 'PGHOST:PGPORT:PGUSER:PGPASSWORD:PGDATABASE:PGSSLMODE:PGSSLROOTCERT:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS' - DATABASE_URL is deliberately absent, and nothing unnamed in WSLENV crosses the Windows/WSL boundary. So the respelled DSN lives only in the direct wsl.exe process and dies there. On the WSL side packages/db/lib/pg.mjs connConfig() finds no URL var and returns {}, so node-postgres builds TLS from the environment: node_modules/.pnpm/pg@8.20.0/node_modules/pg/lib/connection-parameters.js readSSLConfigFromEnvironment() maps PGSSLMODE='verify-full' to plain `true` - no `ca` - i.e. the global trust store augmented by NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (ADDITIVE), not the exclusive DSN pin the module's own header calls the whole point ('a DSN-level pin is what makes node-postgres treat the CA as EXCLUSIVE rather than merely additional'). packages/db/scripts/backup.mjs:140 DOES open such a client on the --profile full path AC1 names. libpq (pg_dump) is unaffected - PGSSLROOTCERT is exclusive for it. NOT A REGRESSION: the hand wrapper this replaces also omitted DATABASE_URL (RELEASE-RUNBOOK-0225-0233.md:213), but it is now shipped behaviour rather than a one-off. packages/db/README.md's new paragraph justifies the omission with 'only the WSL-side client tools need the PG* vars' - inaccurate, since a node pg client connects there too.
findings.required_fix: Say it where an operator reads it: one sentence in packages/db/README.md's #917 paragraph (and in dsn-pipe.mjs's WSL_ENV_LIST header) recording that under --child-os wsl the WSL side authenticates TLS from PGSSLMODE + PGSSLROOTCERT (exclusive for libpq) and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (additive for Node), NOT from the DSN's own sslrootcert pin, and that backup.mjs's node client on that side is in the additive case. If end-to-end exclusivity is actually wanted, that is a successor contract (cross a DSN, or have the WSL side rebuild one from PG* + PGSSLROOTCERT), not a doc fix.

findings.title: WSL_ENV_LIST drops CLARA_BACKUP_DIR, which the wrapper it replaces carried - and the runbook now tells the next ceremony there is no wrapper
findings.evidence: Ticket AC4: "both release runbooks' step-3f invocation are updated to the new flag", and AC1 asks the documented command to succeed "with no wrapper script". The wrapper being retired set `export WSLENV='PGHOST:PGPORT:PGUSER:PGPASSWORD:PGDATABASE:PGSSLMODE:PGSSLROOTCERT/p:CLARA_BACKUP_DIR/p'` (docs/plan/active/refresh-wave-2026-09-18/RELEASE-RUNBOOK-0225-0233.md:213, quoted verbatim in the diff's own kept-as-history paragraph). The shipped WSL_ENV_LIST has the six PG vars plus the two CA vars and NO CLARA_BACKUP_DIR. packages/db/scripts/backup.mjs:54 reads `process.env.CLARA_BACKUP_DIR || join(PKG_ROOT, 'backups')`, so an operator who sets CLARA_BACKUP_DIR on the Windows side and follows the runbook's new wrapper-free invocation silently gets the default directory instead. The dump still succeeds (the default resolves to a WSL-visible /mnt path) - it just does not land where the operator asked.
findings.required_fix: Either add CLARA_BACKUP_DIR to WSL_ENV_LIST with the /p translation flag (it is NOT pre-respelled by dsn-pipe, unlike the two CA vars), or state in the runbook's Update (#917) block and packages/db/README.md that CLARA_BACKUP_DIR does not cross and the artefact lands under packages/db/backups on the WSL side.

findings.title: The cn strip is skipped silently when the pinned CLI exits non-zero - and that CLI installs dependencies BEFORE it writes files, so exactly the hand-revert #969 abolishes survives that path
findings.evidence: Ticket AC1: "Running `ui:add` for an item whose resolution names `cn` leaves no `cn` entry in any `package.json` or in the lockfile, with no manual revert." apps/web/scripts/ui-add.mjs main(): `const code = spawnAdd(argv); if (code !== 0) return code;` - returns before stripLocalDependencies with no message at all, in contrast with the failed-strip path two lines below which logs a loud WARNING naming cn. ORDERING MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: in the pinned shadcn 4.19.0 bundle apps/web/node_modules/shadcn/dist/chunk-CDOZT3OO.js the add flow `yh()` runs `await on(s.dependencies, s.devDependencies, t, ...)` - the function whose spinner reads 'Installing dependencies.' - FIRST, and only then Br (tailwind config), cn (env vars), un (fonts) and the file writer. So a failure in the file-writing half of an add leaves cn already in package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml. No cell covers this branch (the 8 #969 cells cover success, dry-run, override, non-cn, protected-first and failed-strip). apps/web/components/ui/README.md's new window paragraph names 'a killed process, a crashed machine' but not an ordinary non-zero CLI exit.
findings.required_fix: Strip (or at minimum warn, in the same loud shape as the failed-strip path) when spawnAdd returns non-zero and local dependencies were classified, and add the cell: spawnAdd -> 1 with cn in the resolution asserts either the strip call or the WARNING. Cite the measured CLI ordering in the code comment so the next reader need not re-derive it from the bundle.

findings.title: AC2's 'a subsequent verify reports no RETIRED-* violation' is evidenced against a verifier that cannot emit three of the four invariants the ticket names, and no cell drives a successful --retire through the CLI at all

The four the ticket names live in a DIFFERENT verifier - check-frozen-workflows.mjs's own verify path at lines 424 (RETIRED-DUPLICATE), 428 (RETIRED-NO-HASH), 432 (RETIRED-NO-RULING) and 437 (RETIRED-PRESENT). Three of the four are therefore unexercised by the cell that claims them. Separately, the two CLI-spawning cells cover only REFUSALS; the successful --retire write path (the writeFileSync(MANIFEST_PATH, ...) block in main()) has no cell. findings.title: The new lint message never states the 3/4/6/8-hex-character trip condition the ticket's Desired behaviour asks for, and the lane report claims it does
findings.evidence: Ticket Desired behavior: "The rule's message explicitly states that any `#` immediately followed by 3, 4, 6 or 8 hex-looking characters trips this selector, including a ticket reference such as `#658`". SHIPPED TEXT (eslint.config.mjs): 'NOTE: this selector cannot tell a real colour from any other short hex-looking token after `#` - a plain ticket reference like `#658` trips it too (#994). If that is your case, the fix is to REWORD the string (e.g. spell it out as "ticket 658"), never to weaken this rule.' - 'short hex-looking token', never 3/4/6/8. The lane's own report asserts the opposite: 'states any `#` + 3/4/6/8 hex-looking chars trips the selector'. The omission is substantive, not cosmetic: without the counts a developer cannot tell why #658 and #1013 fire while #12345 does not, which is precisely the diagnosis round-trip the ticket exists to abolish. The AC checkbox ('names the ticket-reference case (# followed by digits) and states the recommended fix') IS met, so this is partial, not missing.
findings.required_fix: Add the counts to the message - e.g. '... any `#` immediately followed by 3, 4, 6 or 8 hex-looking characters ...' - and correct the claim in the lane report.
